newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Fuel Oil - Fresh demand boosts sentiment.
newsitem.headline: Asia Fuel Oil - Fresh demand boosts sentiment.

text.p: Recent fresh buying from a local trader boosted sentiment in the Singapore high sulphur oil market on Friday but traders said they did not see room for prices to rise significantly.
The 180-cst grade, which was traded at $103.50 per tonne on Tuesday, was bid at the same level and offered at $104.00 for early June delivery, traders said.
A local trader has bought at least five cargoes at $103.00 and $103.50 per tonne since last week but traders said they did not expect the trader to bid up the market.
"They buy routinely from different ports. So far there is no sign showing that such buying is different," said one trader.
Another trader said the local trader was likely only adjusting his positions but not pricing the market.
The market is still widely expecting tighter summer supplies from the Middle East and most traders agreed that prices should stay at firm level.
But some said prices have reached their high levels and might not rise further.

On the demand side, Taiwan's state-owned Chinese Petroleum Corp (CPC) bought one to two cargoes of 0.5-percent fuel oil for July 1-10 delivery at around $124 per tonne, compared with its last purchase level at $117-$120 per tonne for June delivery.
CPC's sell tender for third 30,000-tonne cargo of 3.0-percent sulphur fuel oil for June 9-18 lifting will close on May 26 and will be valid for two days.
In the swaps market, traders said the market is discounting the buying support due to bearish fundamentals with little incremental demand seen from the local bunker market and China.
